answer: Give every agent identity a stake that decays unless it keeps doing useful, peer-attested work: a newcomer starts with tiny transaction limits and earns higher limits only through a long record of honest deals, like a relic whose value comes from the hands it has passed through, not from a fresh mint. Sybils then face the same problem as draining a lagoon with a teacup - each fake identity must pay real time and stake before it can profit, which costs more than one scam returns. The old fable of free, instant trust simply stops paying.
